sections.h2: Who values and bills a house in Paterson, NJ?
sections.html:
In Paterson the Tax Assessor's Office values every parcel, and the city's tax collector sends the bill. The assessor's page says its job covers appraising land and buildings under state statute, keeping ownership and transfer records current, checking building permits and maintaining values. The same office approves veteran, senior and disabled deductions and puts together the added and omitted assessment list.

City Hall is at 155 Market Street, and the assessor's page lists office hours of Monday through Friday, 8:30 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. Assessment appeals go to the Passaic County Board of Taxation in Totowa, and the assessor represents the city at those hearings and in New Jersey Tax Court. For a due date or a payoff amount on a specific parcel, ask the Paterson tax collector at City Hall for the figure in writing.

sections.h2: What does Paterson look like for a seller?
sections.html:
Paterson is the largest city in Passaic County and dense: 8.41 square miles of land and 18,986 people per square mile in the 2020 Census, with a 2025 estimate of 161,793 residents. The Great Falls of the Passaic River, 77 feet high, powered the mills that earned it the name Silk City, and the Society for Establishing Useful Manufactures founded the town in 1791. It was incorporated as a city in 1851.

Census QuickFacts for 2020 to 2024 gives a median owner-occupied value of $360,100, a median gross rent of $1,548 and a median household income of $55,997. Only 26.9% of housing is owner-occupied, so many Paterson sellers are small landlords with two-, three- or four-family houses. The city has 49,865 households averaging 3.15 people, and 44.6% of residents were born outside the United States.

Paterson borders Clifton, Haledon, Hawthorne, Prospect Park, Totowa and Woodland Park in Passaic County and Elmwood Park and Fair Lawn in Bergen County. Interstate 80 runs through it and the Garden State Parkway passes through the south. The city also contains the Great Falls historic district and the Eastside Park historic district.

sections.h2: Did Paterson revalue homes for 2026, and how do I appeal?
sections.html:
Yes. The Passaic County Board of Taxation lists Paterson as a town that underwent a revaluation or reassessment for 2026, which moved its appeal deadline from April 1 to May 1 that year. That deadline has passed for 2026, but the same pattern applies after any later citywide revaluation.

  • A regular appeal goes to the county board by April 1, or 45 days after bulk mailing of assessment notices, whichever is later.
  • An assessment over $1,000,000 can go directly to the Tax Court of New Jersey.
  • Added and omitted assessments are appealed before December 1.
  • A county board judgment can be taken to Tax Court within 45 days.

The board's guidance says not to file until the assessment card has arrived, which is after February 1. After a revaluation, assessments are meant to equal market value as of the prior October 1, so recent Paterson sales before that date are the best evidence. Added or omitted assessment bills are generally sent in October and payable November 1.

sections.h2: Which deductions can lower a Paterson tax bill?
sections.html:
The assessor's page lists three local benefits, each applied for through the assessor with a claim form. The deductions reduce the bill for qualified owners, and the exemption removes it for a narrow group.

Paterson Tax Assessor deductions and exemptions, per the city's published eligibility notes
BenefitAmountMain eligibility testClaim form
Veteran or surviving spouse deduction$250 a yearOwner and New Jersey resident on October 1 of the pre-tax year; qualifying wartime or peacekeeping serviceV.S.S.
Senior, disabled or surviving spouse deduction$250 a yearAge 65 or older, or permanently disabled, as of December 31; income under $10,000 excluding certain benefitsPTD
Disabled veteran exemptionFull exemption of home and lotCertified 100% permanently and totally disabled by the VA; owner and residentD.V.S.S.E.

Veteran applicants need a copy of the DD-214. The disabled veteran claim can be filed at any time of year. State programs such as ANCHOR and Senior Freeze are separate, and the 2025 application deadline of November 2, 2026 has passed.

sections.h2: How does Paterson's local economy bear on home values?
sections.html:
Paterson's workforce is large and local. Census QuickFacts shows 63.6% of residents 16 and older in the civilian labor force and a mean commute of 22.6 minutes, shorter than in Old Bridge or Ocean County. Health care and social assistance receipts reached about $1.37 billion in 2022, and retail sales were about $1.56 billion, or $9,981 per resident, a lower per-capita figure than Passaic County overall.

The poverty rate was 21.2% and the share of residents without health insurance under 65 was 21.3%, so many owners have limited room to absorb a surprise tax bill. A homeowner who falls behind on a first quarter installment should talk to the collector early, because the interest clock starts on the due date and the debt grows with each missed quarter.

sections.h2: What happens if Paterson property tax goes unpaid?
sections.html:
Paterson sells unpaid tax liens at an online auction. The city's notice for the sale of 2023 delinquent taxes and municipal charges set the bidding for December 11, 2024 at 10:00 a.m. on the city's New Jersey tax sale site. Parcel lists and bidding instructions are free to view.

State law allows an accelerated sale when taxes or liens are still open on the 11th day of the eleventh month of the fiscal year. Interest on late installments is set by the city, at no more than 8% a year on the first $1,500 and 18% above it, and the city may allow ten days of grace. A seller facing a lien should know that a tax sale certificate is a recorded claim against the parcel, and it has to be redeemed or cancelled to clear title.

  • Ask the collector for a payoff letter good through the closing date.
  • Ask the Passaic County Clerk whether any tax sale certificate is on record.
  • Redeem the certificate before closing so title is clear.

sections.h2: What else should a Paterson seller check before listing?
sections.html:
Ask the city for open permits and violations before you list. The Passaic River flooded badly in August 2011 after Hurricane Irene, with water at levels not seen in 100 years, and buyers may ask about past water in basements. The Paterson School District covers all the area inside the city limits.

The Passaic County Clerk records the deed, at $45 for the first page and $10 for each added page, and the county fee schedule also gives the realty transfer tax rates by price band. The assessor keeps transfer records, so ownership on the tax roll updates after the deed is recorded.

faqs.q: Where is the Paterson Tax Assessor's Office?
faqs.a: It is in City Hall at 155 Market Street, Paterson, NJ. The city lists hours of Monday through Friday, 8:30 a.m. to 4:30 p.m.

faqs.q: When was the Paterson appeal deadline for 2026?
faqs.a: May 1, 2026, because Paterson underwent a revaluation or reassessment that year. The deadline for a regular appeal in other towns is April 1, and that window for 2026 has closed.

faqs.q: How much is the Paterson veteran property tax deduction?
faqs.a: It is $250 a year for a qualified veteran or surviving spouse who owns the home and lived in New Jersey on October 1 of the pre-tax year. A disabled veteran certified 100% permanently and totally disabled by the VA can claim a full exemption.
Yes. The city sold 2023 delinquent taxes in an online auction on December 11, 2024. Parcel details are posted on the city's New Jersey tax sale page.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Paterson house that owes property tax?
faqs.a: Yes. Taxes and interest are paid from the proceeds at closing. Get a payoff letter from the Paterson tax collector, and clear any tax sale certificate before the closing date.
